title: Algebraic extinction in acyclic spreading models: explicit counterexamples, genericity and support-checkable repairs
creator: Anonymous

statusLabels.proof: complete written argument in the paper, not machine-checked
statusLabels.exact: symbolic or exact-rational computation reproduced by the package

source.reference: Chan, K. M. D., Crommelin, D. T., and Mandjes, M. R. H. (2025). Asymptotic behavior for a general class of spreading models. arXiv:2511.02437v1 (only version as of 2026-10-21). Conjecture 1, p. 25.

parentRelease.title: Algebraic extinction in acyclic compartment models
parentRelease.relation: Earlier release by the same publisher (Evidence Press). It refutes Conjecture 1 (18/t^2, cyclic dependency graph); same minimality statement; family with exponents m/(m-1); classification of its own four-state model; same limiting-Jacobian log-rate theorem. This paper is a successor.

claims.statement: A no-direct-infection SWIR/GEP submodel (Janssen-Muller-Stenull 2004, Sec. II), with recovery encoded as in source eq. (8), satisfies Assumptions 1-2 and admits a tricritical-type triple zero; interior data give x ~ (sqrt(3)/8) t^-3/2 (nu=eta=4). Not identified with the tricritical point analysed by Janssen et al.
s'=-2sx, w'=2sx-wx, x'=(w-r)x, r'=rx; data (25/48,5/24,1/240,4/15); both graphs acyclic; x ~ sqrt(3/8) t^-3/2; derived from a triple root of the exposure cubic.
Same model, data (50/81,25/162,11/3240,9/40), x ~ 4 t^-2; codimension one.
N<=3 under (G1)-(G2) with interior data implies exponential decay.
Even m: (m+2)-state chain with both graphs acyclic, x ~ C_m t^(-1-1/m); odd m fails (m=3 gives x0=-1/6048).
Only for y'=xHy: zero order <= 2*floor(N/2)-1, sharp (odd N by duplicating the terminal compartment).

Any N=4 model under (G1)-(G2) with interior data: each vanishing coordinate is exponential, ~C t^-2 or ~C t^-3/2; nothing slower (Theorem 5.7). Two-vanishing-state examples near t^-3/2 and t^-2 are numerical (Remark 5.8).
Four-state chain, all rates and interior data: exponential, 2/(kappa t^2), or sqrt(3)/(2 sqrt(alpha beta gamma)) t^-3/2.
y'=xHy: exponential set open, algebraic set null; order>=k set has codimension r_k<=k-1; chain codimensions 1 and 2.
Order-k zero, perturbation with g!=0: rate k a_k^(1/k) |eps g|^((k-1)/k), endpoint shift |eps|^(1/k); one-sided jump for even k.
x strictly decreasing for multiple-zero trajectories of the chain (all rates), SWIR, and the hierarchy.
Under (G1): lim (1/t) log||v|| = s(J); exponential iff s(J)<0. A posteriori; standard tools.

Acyclic limiting influence graph and no autocatalytic inflow from persistent donors imply exponential decay; checkable from supports once labels are known (source Corollary 1 identifiability condition).
Acyclic influence graph and c_kii <= h_ik (strict for some k) imply exponential decay; rates alone cannot decide an individual trajectory without its initial data.
Gillespie simulation, N=2.4e4..2.4e7: median extinction ~ 1.48 N^0.42 (95% bootstrap [0.38,0.46]).

exclusions: No historical-priority claim; the conjecture is already refuted in the prior release.
Minimality and the limiting-block theorem restate results of the prior release.
The exponent 3/2, the exposure clock and Metzler/Perron-Frobenius tools are not claimed as new.
The limiting-block theorem is an a posteriori criterion that needs the limit.
No empirical data; critical data are tuned.
